profiles.question: What exactly crosses the front/core binding, what can a malicious upload make core do, and how long do uploads live?
evidence: src/front/index.ts serveLimited: non-/api paths go to ASSETS; /api requests pass the full Request (method, headers incl. cf-connecting-ip, body) to CORE.fetch after one rate-limit check.
src/worker/index.ts route: core accepts only /api/recordings (GET list, POST upload), /api/recordings/:id, /api/recordings/:id/narrate. ids must match ^[a-z0-9-]{3,64}$.
Core work per upload: one D1 count, one D1 insert, ceil(steps/64) Clef calls, two R2 puts, one D1 upsert. Retention: no expiry (README Limits).

findings.finding: store.ts saveRecording wrote the unredacted raw log to R2 raw/<id>.log, while README and page copy say host names and home paths are replaced.
readUpload treated a missing content-length as 0, so a chunked body was read fully into memory before the 5 MB check.
Core is reachable only by service binding (workers_dev false, no routes in core/wrangler.prod.jsonc), so it trusts cf-connecting-ip from front.
findings.reason: No public route to core. Cloudflare sets cf-connecting-ip at the edge.

Spoofed cf-connecting-ip header to live: Cloudflare returned error code 1000 (403). The limiter key comes from the edge value.
